skeleton:
Chermoula — The Marinade of the Sea

Moroccan · Easy · Makes about 200 ml (one batch; marinades 1 kg fish)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The chermoula is the sea's own marinade — the parsley-cilantro-garlic-cumin-paprika paste with the preserved lemon's pulp and the lemon juice's brightness, pounded (or processed) to the thick wet rub that the fish pots (#37, #90) and the sardine's fillings (#29) run on. It is less a recipe than a grammar: the herbs' ratio, the acid's law, and the two-stage use (the marinade's coat, the sauce's rebuild).

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

  • or the fresh lemon's juice's doubled mercy
- **The chermoula's law: it is used twice — the coat and the rebuild.** The paste's first half runs the fish's 30-minute marinade (the acid's surface work, the oil's perfume carry); the second half goes into the pot itself (the #37's sauce base, the #90's poaching broth's body), because the marinade's escaped juices and the pot's rebuild together run the whole flavor's economy — the single-use marinade wastes half the grammar. - **The bridge:** the #92's two-faces law runs the record's own hinge (the pulp's mash here, the peel's threads at the service), and the #29 sardine roll and the #37 fish tagine carry this jar's every downstream application.

Chermoula — The Marinade of the Sea

Prep: 15 min · Cook: No cook · Total: 15 min · Makes about 200 ml (one batch; marinades 1 kg fish)

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 1 large bunch cilantro (about 30 g) and 1 bunch parsley (about 30 g), the tender leaves and stems' top third
  • 5 garlic cloves (about 20 g)
  • 1 tsp ground cumin and 1 tsp sweet paprika (about 5 g total)
  • ½ tsp ground coriander
  • ¼ tsp cayenne or 1 tsp harissa (#91)
  • 1 preserved lemon's pulp (#92), mashed (about 15 g) — or the fresh lemon's juice's doubled mercy
  • Juice of 1 lemon (about 45 ml)
  • 90 ml olive oil (about 82 g)
  • 1 tsp salt (about 6 g)

Instructions

  1. **The paste (10 minutes).** The herbs, garlic, spices, preserved-lemon pulp, lemon juice, salt, and oil pounded in the mortar (the traditional order: the garlic and salt first to the paste, the spices worked in, the herbs last to the bruised green) or pulsed in the processor to the coarse, wet, granular-smooth rub. Checkpoint — the paste's proof: thick and wet — a rub's body, not a sauce's pour — the herbs' green dominant at the eye and the garlic-cumin's warmth dominant at the nose; the taste on the fingertip: bright, salty, the preserved lemon's fermented depth under the fresh juice's snap (the two citruses' marriage is the true chermoula's own signature).
  2. **The marinade's coat (30 minutes, the fish's law).** The first half of the paste worked over the fish's every face — the cavity, the fillet's flesh-side, the steaks' faces — and the fish held chilled 30 minutes and no longer. Checkpoint — the 30-minute law's edge: the marinade's acid runs the surface's work at the half-hour's mark (the flesh's outer proteins' faint whitening, the perfume's penetration); the hour-plus marinade runs the acid's overwork — the cured-ceviche's texture's edge at the surface, the chalk's beginning — and the chermoula's whole grammar keeps the fish at the market's own freshness.
  3. **The pot's rebuild.** The second half's destiny: the #37's sauce (the paste fried briefly in the oil's shimmer before the tomatoes' entry), the #90's broth's body, or the grill's basting — the record's own economy running whole. Checkpoint — eating test (the marinated, grilled fillet's first proof): the chermoula's perfume run through the fish's surface — the herbs' green, the cumin's warmth, the two lemons' married brightness — the flesh within still the sea's own sweetness, the marinade's work present but never the cure's aggression. It should taste like the coast's own answer to the fire — the sea seasoned, not the sea overwritten.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Marinade's taste flat, one-note sourThe fresh juice onlyThe #92 pulp's marriage — the two-citrus law
Paste bitterThe herbs' stems' lower halfThe tender top-third's law
Fish's surface whitened, chalkyThe marinade's hour-plusThe 30-minute edge

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The paste keeps 3 days refrigerated under the oil's thin seal — the make-ahead's own mercy, the Friday paste and the Saturday fish — and the full batch's doubling runs the week's whole sea. The variations: the raisin-and-cinnamon's sweet register (the #36's cousin for the fish tagine's sweet dial), the saffron's thread's addition for the ceremony's pot, the cilantro-only's Tunisian honesty.
